formulas.title: Scalar Gaussian forward-KL risk
formulas.plain: The expected predictive log-loss penalty for estimating an unknown Gaussian variance has a finite closed form only above its inverse-moment threshold.

variables.meaning: expected forward Kullback–Leibler divergence in nats

conditions: True observations IID N(0,v*),v*>0; mean known.
MLE uses divisor n; forward direction true distribution to fitted distribution; n>2.
limitingCases: E_n→0 as n→∞ under correct specification.
pitfalls: Reverse KL is a different expectation.
A two-point calculation illustrates but does not prove all-n monotonicity.

formulas.title: Finite benchmark scoring convention
formulas.plain: The reported count applies a threshold to averaged referee scores, not a trusted-kernel decision.
conditions: Use First ProofBatch3 rubric and ten tasks.
limitingCases: A score.5 is counted despite incomplete confidence.
pitfalls: Do not read3/10 as three fully machine-certified proofs.
These tasks are not a random sample of all mathematics.
Under the stricter mean-grade-equals1 convention, Siege has2/10; that alternate count is not the report’s published total.

formulas.title: Permanent definition
formulas.plain: Sum one product per permutation, without determinant signs.

variables.meaning: square matrix over a commutative field

conditions: Square n×n matrix; a commutative coefficient field.
derivation: Each permutation chooses one entry from every row and column.
All chosen products are added with coefficient+1.
limitingCases: Diagonal matrices give the product of diagonal entries.
pitfalls: Definition does not establish any claimed circuit lower bound.
Arithmetic model and coefficient field matter for complexity.

formulas.title: ε-light set definition
formulas.plain: Every quadratic energy of induced edges is bounded by ε times the original graph energy.
conditions: Finite undirected graph and compatible nonnegative edge weights.
PSD order refers to all real vectors, not entrywise inequalities.
derivation: Laplacian energy is sum over edges of w_uv(z_u−z_v)².
Subtract induced-edge energy from ε times total.

steps: Induced graph has no edges, soL_S=0.
workedExample.result: SingletonS is ε-light; both vertices are not forε<1.

pitfalls: Checking one test vector is insufficient.
This example does not prove the universal large-subset theorem.

glossary.definition: Large language model: a text-generating model, not itself a proof certificate.
Nesterov accelerated gradient; algorithm schedules and problem hypotheses must be specified.
Maximum likelihood estimator; parameter maximizing the observed-data likelihood.
Kullback–Leibler divergence; directional expected log likelihood ratio, not a symmetric distance.
Independent and identically distributed observations.
A proof assistant with a small trusted kernel; source code is not a successful checking receipt.
Lean project/build manager, with dependency/toolchain configuration.
Artifact described in linked instructions for additional theorem/statement checking; not executed here.
An assumed statement; consistency and intended interpretation limit the scope of a checked proof.
Lean placeholder that can admit a proposition; absence must be checked in the relevant dependency closure.
Software orchestrating model calls, tools and stopping; not interchangeable with the underlying model.
International Mathematical Olympiad; contest problems and medal-level scores do not imply new theorems.
American Invitational Mathematics Examination; a short-answer benchmark when reused in model evaluation, not a new-theorem collection.
Program with separately specified tiered answer tasks, open-problem tasks and formal Erdős tasks.
Positive semidefinite; a symmetric matrix has nonnegative quadratic form for every real vector.
CANDECOMP/PARAFAC tensor decomposition by alternating least squares.
Preconditioned conjugate gradient, an iterative linear solver requiring suitable definiteness hypotheses.
Reproducing kernel Hilbert space; a function space whose evaluation is represented by a kernel.
Away from specified algebraic exceptional sets; not simply a random numerical example.
Admitting finite permutation approximations in the specified asymptotic sense.
Field-like algebra with multivalued addition; ordinary polynomial identities need not transfer as naive implications.
Smallest complete-graph size forcing a monochromatic structure under every allowed edge coloring.
An algebraic computation graph; different from a Boolean circuit or a formula with no shared subcomputations.
An algorithmic complexity notion controlling arithmetic-operation count independently of input coefficient bit magnitudes, with additional size requirements.
Matrix multiplication exponent, an infimum of feasible arithmetic asymptotic exponents; equality needs both upper and lower reasoning.
Public manuscript without an implied completed journal review.
A review or experiment with a distinct evidential role; company hosting, expert fame or institutional funding alone does not certify a result.
Precisely which sections were inspected; download size does not measure review completeness.
Group of invertible r×r matrices over fieldF; N_r is its upper-triangular unipotent subgroup, with diagonal entries1.
A realization of a generic representation by functions with specified character equivariance under a unipotent subgroup; its character and representation hypotheses are part of First ProofProblem2.
A locally compact field with a non-archimedean valuation; its ring of integers and conductor ideals enter the local Rankin–Selberg question.

openQuestions.question: Do the selected Lean certificates check the intended historical statements?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Pinned toolchain/import closure, no-placeholder check, printed axiom dependencies, clean kernel/comparator execution.

openQuestions.question: Are November24 LP and matrix-exponent claims correct and novel?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Original papers, exact statements, independent domain experts, artifact builds and prior-art comparison.

openQuestions.question: What is the independent current status of Erdős183?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Reachable database snapshot or maintainer confirmation; current direct page returned403.

openQuestions.question: How should AI help and concurrent proofs be credited in NAG?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Read concurrent paper13 and full revision chronology, not just provider interview.

openQuestions.question: How do qualified reviewer judgments and the dimension-context mismatch affect the exact Darcy claim?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Organizer errata plus complete proof and report scope, including rate formula and missing steps.

openQuestions.question: Which specific October collection claims have independent favorable or unfavorable reviews?
openQuestions.neededEvidence: Claim-level MathHelm commentary with author identity and exact manuscript version.

claims.problemStatement: For convex L-smooth f:R^n→R with an attained minimum, establish point convergence x_k,y_k→x∞∈argmin f for the paper’s classical NAG parameter schedules; also critical-damping continuous-time convergence.
claims.priorStatus: Authors describe a longstanding point-convergence question, distinct from already-known objective-value O(k^-2) convergence.
claims.AIContribution: Ryu reports repeated prompting, rejection of faulty suggestions and a structurally useful but incorrect-as-written proposal; Jang/Ryu developed and wrote the proof.
claims.verificationStatus: Author-checked preprint, arXivv2 January19 2026; full proof not independently verified here.
claims.independentEvidence: Paper Section1.3 reports a concurrent discrete-time proof prompted by the October21 public post, with additional Hilbert/FISTA results. No separate concurrent paper was read.
claims.limitations: Do not turn human-directed collaboration into autonomous solving, or mathematical point convergence into universal algorithm stability.

claims.problemStatement: For IID N(0,Σ*) samples in dimensiond, Σ*>0, prove expected forward KL risk of covariance MLE strictly decreases for n>d+1, and is infinite for n≤d+1; paper extends to unknown mean and other families.
claims.priorStatus: Paper traces the correctly specified Gaussian question to2019/2022 learning-curve work; reverse-KL extension partly reconnects to a known textbook exercise.
claims.AIContribution: Authors say model supplied proof strategies without human intermediate scaffolding; humans prompted extensions, checked and transcribed; model later located relevant prior art.
claims.verificationStatus: Human-author verification and provider-reported external review; no journal verdict or machine proof run established.
claims.independentEvidence: Original Sellke/Yin manuscript inspected for exact theorem and assistance statement, but it is the same collaboration rather than an independent replication.
claims.limitations: More data is not universally beneficial under misspecification; forward/reverse KL and finite-risk thresholds differ.

claims.problemStatement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field with ring of integers o; let N_r be the upper-triangular unipotent subgroup of GL_r(F). Fix a nontrivial additive character ψ of conductor o and a generic irreducible admissible representation Π of GL_(n+1)(F) in W(Π,ψ^(-1)). Must there exist one W in that Whittaker model such that, for every generic irreducible admissible π of GL_n(F) in W(π,ψ), with conductor idealq, generatorQ of q^(-1), and u_Q=I_(n+1)+Q E_(n,n+1), some V∈W(π,ψ) makes ∫_(N_n\GL_n(F)) W(diag(g,1)u_Q)V(g)|det g|^(s−1/2)dg finite and nonzero for every s∈C?
claims.priorStatus: A hidden-solution research benchmark question, not evidence that all relevant theory was globally unsolved.
claims.AIContribution: Internal model generated/typeset attempt; humans selected attempts and requested clarification based on feedback.
claims.verificationStatus: Provider explicitly corrected its initial likely-correct assessment to incorrect.
claims.independentEvidence: OpenAI cites organizer commentary and community analysis; selected organizer text inspected, not an independent re-derivation of this attempt.
claims.limitations: The order of quantifiers matters: one W is selected before varying π; V may depend on π. The representation-theoretic setup is reproduced from organizer Problem2. This record audits an explicitly corrected attempt, not a solved theorem.

claims.problemStatement: For monic real-rooted degree-n polynomials p,q with the organizer’s finite free additive convolution, is 1/Φ_n(p⊞_n q)≥1/Φ_n(p)+1/Φ_n(q), with Φ_n(p)=Σ_{i≤n}Σ_{j≠i}(1/(λ_i−λ_j))² and Φ=∞ at repeated roots?
claims.priorStatus: Research-level hidden-solution challenge; prior human solutions existed.
claims.AIContribution: Model-generated proof attempt, human best-of selection and clarification.
claims.verificationStatus: Company reports high chance of correctness, not a machine-checked theorem verdict.
claims.independentEvidence: Organizer provides exact statement; its early GPT-5.2 baseline comments do not grade this later internal-model attempt.
claims.limitations: Polynomial normalization and repeated-root conventions matter; complete proof not independently audited. The Φ definition is transcribed as the source’s double sum of squared reciprocals.

claims.problemStatement: Does a universal c>0 exist such that every finite graph and 0<ε<1 admit S⊂V with |S|≥cε|V| and L_S≼εL, where L_S retains only edges insideS?
claims.priorStatus: Hidden human-solved spectral graph question in First Proof.
claims.AIContribution: Generated proof with limited human supervision and expert-feedback clarification.
claims.verificationStatus: Provider provisional high-confidence result.
claims.independentEvidence: Organizer statement inspected; no independent verification of this exact internal attempt obtained.
claims.limitations: A sampled graph experiment cannot prove the universal existence claim; PSD means positive-semidefinite order.

claims.problemStatement: For n≥5 and Zariski-generic A^(α)∈R^(3×4), find n-independent-degree polynomial relations recognizing exactly the coordinatewise tensor scalings λ_αβγδ=u_αv_βw_γx_δ of determinant tensors, with the organizer’s nonzero-pattern restriction.
claims.priorStatus: Hidden-solution algebraic research challenge.
claims.AIContribution: Generated candidate argument; humans selected and formatted outputs.
claims.verificationStatus: Provider high-chance assessment; proof not independently checked here.
claims.independentEvidence: Exact organizer problem and internal submitted section9 retrieved.
claims.limitations: Genericity, exceptional index pattern and if-and-only-if direction must survive formalization; omitted zero cases can change the question.

claims.problemStatement: Explain a matrix-free preconditioned conjugate-gradient method for the stated nr×nr kernelized CP-ALS normal system with missing tensor entries, selection matrixS, Kronecker products and RKHS kernelK.
claims.priorStatus: Research-method benchmark with existing human solution.
claims.AIContribution: Model-generated linear-algebra derivation and proof attempt, selected under human supervision.
claims.verificationStatus: Provider high chance of correctness; implementation/runtime advantage not independently reproduced.
claims.independentEvidence: Organizer system equation and requested preconditioner/matvec explanation inspected.
claims.limitations: Positive-semidefinite versus definite operators, regularization and solver convergence hypotheses cannot be inferred from an equation label.

claims.problemStatement: For k-colour triangle Ramsey numberR_k(3), claim logR_k(3)=Θ(k logk), hence R_k(3)^(1/k)→∞; reported as resolving Erdős183.
claims.priorStatus: Longstanding superexponential-growth question according to announcement/manuscript; direct current database access blocked.
claims.AIContribution: Provider says model generated argument; humans/model prepared manuscript and Lean certificate.
claims.verificationStatus: Provider-reported formalization; manuscript and selected actual Lean declarations inspected. No Lean kernel, dependency-axiom audit or Comparator execution was performed; proof correctness is not independently certified.
claims.independentEvidence: No claim-specific independent correctness verdict located; code existence and MathHelm’s broad response are different evidence types.
claims.limitations: Do not label accepted solely from provider formalization claim; exact theorem/imports/axioms need pinned build and comparison.

claims.problemStatement: Claim vol(K)≤(n+1)^n/n! for convex bodies K⊂R^n whose centroid is the unique interior lattice point, in the stated lattice-volume convention.
claims.priorStatus: Ehrhart volume conjecture according to authors.
claims.AIContribution: Generated proof, human-assisted manuscript preparation, claimed Lean formalization.
claims.verificationStatus: Announcement and manuscript abstract read; proof module/build not audited.
claims.independentEvidence: No independent claim-specific proof review captured.
claims.limitations: Convex-body hypotheses and lattice normalization are essential; graph node is a documented claim, not certified resolution.

claims.problemStatement: Claim division-free arithmetic circuit lower boundΩ(n²loglogn) and arithmetic-formula leaf lower boundΩ(n⁴/logn) for the n×n permanent under the manuscript’s algebraic model.
claims.priorStatus: Claims improvement of arithmetic lower bounds; not itself a P≠NP theorem.
claims.AIContribution: Provider attributes argument to model and preparation/formalization to model plus humans.
claims.verificationStatus: Selected abstract/overview only; no proof or certificate execution.
claims.independentEvidence: No independent verdict located for this exact lower bound.
claims.limitations: Arithmetic circuits, formulas, field and allowed operations differ from Boolean computational complexity.

claims.problemStatement: Claim an explicit countable group which is not sofic, disproving that every countable group admits the required finite permutation approximations.
claims.priorStatus: Major group-theoretic question as identified by authors.
claims.AIContribution: Model-generated construction; manuscript/certificate prepared with human involvement.
claims.verificationStatus: Selected primary claim inspected; no complete construction or proof audit.
claims.independentEvidence: Independent correctness remains unresolved in this selected corpus.
claims.limitations: Existence of a Lean filename is not evidence the mathematical statement matches the historical question.

claims.problemStatement: Three manuscripts on split abelian eightfold Weil classes, Kuga–Satake correspondences for K3 surfaces, and rational Hodge for products of K3 surfaces were withdrawn after a sign-error-dependent construction failed.
claims.priorStatus: October6 release had presented results; history now withdraws these specific manuscripts.
claims.AIContribution: Model-origin outputs entered a large collection; authors maintain corrections/dependency notices.
claims.verificationStatus: Withdrawn by issuer on October7: these three specific manuscripts are not accepted proofs; withdrawal does not apply automatically to other Hodge-related claims.
claims.independentEvidence: Direct revision-history notice captured; root mathematical error not independently reconstructed.
claims.limitations: Do not extend these withdrawals to all Hodge-related papers; later CM-abelian-variety formalization is a different claim.

claims.problemStatement: November24 history claims a deterministic strongly polynomial algorithm for general linear programming, answering Smale’s ninth problem.
claims.priorStatus: Major open complexity question according to issuer.
claims.AIContribution: A newly released model-generated manuscript family; no detailed contribution audit yet.
claims.verificationStatus: Unverified source claim: newly announced; original manuscript unread, independent correctness/novelty checks pending.
claims.independentEvidence: Only history announcement retrieved, not original proof or independent review.
claims.limitations: Lead-level claim deliberately excluded from verified-theorem count; one-day freshness increases review uncertainty.

claims.problemStatement: November24 history lists “The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths,” i.e. claims ω=9/4 in the intended arithmetic asymptotic convention.
claims.priorStatus: Claims an exact exponent, a stronger statement than an upper bound; original theorem hypotheses not read.
claims.AIContribution: Issuer lists new model-origin tensor-geometry manuscripts.
claims.verificationStatus: Unverified source claim: newly announced; original manuscript unread, independent correctness/novelty checks pending.
claims.independentEvidence: No original manuscript or independent result captured.
claims.limitations: Exact equality in a history title must not be silently weakened to a proven algorithmic bound or promoted to established fact.

claims.problemStatement: First Proof Batch3: solve ten researcher-origin questions with hidden pre-existing human solutions under the specified one-shot/no-human-input evaluation.
claims.priorStatus: Unpublished human solutions existed; this is research-proof evaluation, not ten newly open theorem resolutions.
claims.AIContribution: Anthropic provided a workflow; its performance reflects harness, model, budget and abstention policy.
claims.verificationStatus: Independent expert grading: published threshold count3/10 at mean correctness≥0.5; two submissions have mean1 and one has mean0.5 with minor gaps. No submissions for3,4,8,9,10. This is not three strict/unanimous proof acceptances.
claims.independentEvidence: First Proof46-page report, Tables2–5 and detailed reviews inspected.
claims.limitations: Some accepted-threshold submissions have gaps; exposition/attribution separate; no kernel proofs or representative distribution guarantee.

claims.problemStatement: For a hyperfieldH and 0∈x⊞y⊞z, must 0 belong to x³⊞y³⊞z³⊞(−xyz)⊞(−xyz)⊞(−xyz)? Batch3P5 asks this universal implication; submitted answer provides a counterexample.
claims.priorStatus: Human had already solved benchmark problem; reviewers note alternative construction combines prior Connes–Consani and Hall work.
claims.AIContribution: System reconstructed a counterexample using an infinite cyclic projective-plane hyperfield.
claims.verificationStatus: All three referees find mathematics correct; attribution judged deficient, mean attribution0; exposition−.33.
claims.independentEvidence: ReportSections3.5/5.5 inspected, including criticism that reproduced prior constructions need explicit citations.
claims.limitations: A correct counterexample can still be a rediscovery with weak attribution; this does not establish independent first discovery by Claude.

claims.problemStatement: Batch3P2: for div(f∇u)=1 on unit ballD⊂R^d,d≥2, zero boundary data, Yn=u_f+n^(-1/2)W and f in a small C^α-neighbourhood of1, determine minimax L² conductivity-estimation rate up to logarithms.
claims.priorStatus: Hidden human-solved research question; printed context includes an inconsistent d=1 discussion, which must not overwrite the formal d≥2 statement.
claims.AIContribution: Plug-in kernel estimation and Assouad-type lower bound, without human intervention in the recorded run.
claims.verificationStatus: Referees grade correctness.50: sound strategy with minor proof gaps; not an unconditional fully audited theorem.
claims.independentEvidence: ReportSections3.2/5.2 andTable2 read; reviewers flag missing attribution and multivariate notation corrections.
claims.limitations: Exact rate formula not transcribed here because the reviewed passage does not provide it; problem statement and qualified review are recorded, not a fabricated exponent.

claims.problemStatement: First Proof Batch3 ten hidden-human-solution problems under a one-shot24-hour, no-human-input protocol.
claims.priorStatus: Already human-solved unpublished benchmark problems.
claims.AIContribution: Public base-model prompting rather than a separate human-provided proof outline; system and budget are documented.
claims.verificationStatus: Independent First Proof Table2 reports7/10 at mean correctness≥0.5. The stricter alternative of requiring mean grade exactly1 counts5/10. The published7 therefore includes partial/qualified judgments; neither count certifies machine-verified new theorems.
claims.independentEvidence: ReportTable2 and detailed reviews include qualified computational checks; attribution adequate for only4/10.
claims.limitations: Seven includes threshold/qualified judgments; do not compare directly to benchmark percentages with different scoring, sampling or compute.

claims.problemStatement: Answer FrontierMath Tiers1–3 expert-designed problems under provider maximum-effort reasoning with a Python tool.
claims.priorStatus: Benchmark authored with known checkable answers; new/unpublished questions do not necessarily ask globally open theorems.
claims.AIContribution: Model plus tool computation under a declared evaluation setup.
claims.verificationStatus: Provider reports40.3%; no independent rerun captured.
claims.independentEvidence: Original benchmark abstract/current Epoch track distinctions inspected, but they do not independently reproduce this model score.
claims.limitations: A score is not a list of new theorems; track, tools, version and denominator must accompany it.

claims.problemStatement: Solve the six IMO2024 competition problems, with Lean-based formal reasoning on translated statements and a dedicated geometry system.
claims.priorStatus: Competition problems with official solutions/marking, not an open-problem research theorem collection.
claims.AIContribution: Formal-search and geometry systems; humans translated statements, and some computation took much longer than contestant time.
claims.verificationStatus: Provider reports4/6 and28/42 silver-medal-level; formal system claims are source-reported, not rerun here.
claims.independentEvidence: Official technical announcement inspected, not all proof certificates or original problem texts.
claims.limitations: Do not conflate medal-level scoring with actual contest participation or equal time/translation conditions.
